You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like October 2008. VIX is at 46.72 at month-end, which fits October 2008 (about 59.9 at the end of October and 55.7 at the end of November), though it could also be an earlier point. Several other readings fit that period:

- The fed funds rate is 1.56%, an effective rate that averaged about 0.97% in October 2008 and was near 2% in September.
- Headline CPI is 5.36% YoY, which matches the July 2008 peak of 5.6% and September's 4.9%.
- Unemployment is 6.1%, which matches September 2008 (6.1%) and October (6.5%).
- US large-cap equity is down 9.4% in the month and 23.2% over 12 months. September 2008 was about -9.1% for the month, and the 12-month return was about -21.9%.
- Investment-grade credit is down 10.7% in the month, which is a very large drop. It looks like a September–October 2008 episode.
- The 2-year yield of 1.70% fits October 2008 (about 1.56%), and the 10-year at 3.61% fits end-October (about 3.95%).

The trailing figures suggest October. The 3-month equity return of -9.1% and the 1-month return of -9.4% imply that August and July were roughly flat. That fits end-September, since the S&P 500 was down about 9% in September, roughly -8.4% in the quarter and -21.9% over 12 months. For October the monthly return would be about -16.8%, so this does not fit.

Emerging markets fell 14.7% in the month. In September 2008, EM fell about 16%, which is close. The 10y-2y spread of 1.91 is high, though. At the end of September 2008, the 2-year was about 1.96% and the 10-year about 3.83%, a spread of 1.87. That is similar, and the 3-month change of +0.55 in the spread fits too. The VIX at the end of September 2008 was 46.7, which matches exactly.

So the snapshot is September 2008.
